messages:
Elaine Ho: FYI - spotted a weird case where cross-region penalty gets effectively double-applied when the same underlying signal (edge latency) flows into both the 'latency' and 'region-penalty' stages. Seen in traces and in the route-decisions dashboard.

Samir Patel: Can you paste a quick trace snippet? Is it mis-attribution or actual double scoring?

Elaine Ho: snippet below (redacted):
```
route_decision: {
  signals: [
    {src: "edge/nyc/latency_v2", score: 0.8},
    {src: "region/nyc/penalty", score: 0.7}  // derived from same probe stream
  ]
  final_score: 1.5 // looks additive instead of merged
}
```

Elaine Ho: Looks like the policy eval is treating them as orthogonal signals. But they originate from the same measurement pipeline.

Igor Kovacs: If they're literally from the same probe source we should dedupe at signal ingestion. Downside: ingestion-level dedupe is global and brittle for new signal names. Adds cost to stream processing.

Samir Patel: Options I see: 
- ingest sanitization (stream processor) dedupe by probe-id
- policy-compiler normalization (compiler rewrites similar sources into one canonical signal)
- runtime de-dup (policy eval checks a dedupe set per-request)

Liz Chen: Runtime dedupe will increase per-request CPU and memory (we'd keep a short-lived set/bloom). For high QPS tenants that matters. But ingestion fixes the source of truth which is nicer for telemetry later.

Mike Rosario: Product question: do we have customers impacted? Any SLO regressions? If rollout touches ingestion, that's infra change w/ potential data gaps.

Elaine Ho: Two customers surfaced in the dashboard with higher-than-expected penalties in last 48h. SLOs didn't cross alert yet but the cost projections look wrong.

Samir Patel: Architecturally I'd prefer a layered approach: quick runtime guard to stop the worst duplications, plus an ingestion RFC to canonicalize signals long-term. Runtime guard buys time for infra work and smaller blast radius.

Igor Kovacs: Agreed. Runtime guard implementation sketch: keep a dedupe map keyed by origin-probe-id and signal-group hash. Check pseudo-code: 
```python
# in policy eval (hot path)
def score_signals(signals):
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for s in signals:
        key = (s.probe_id, s.group)
        if key in seen:
            s.score = min(s.score, 0.9 * seen_score_for(key))  # dampen duplicate
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        out.append(s)
    return combine(out)
```
This avoids full dedupe but damps duplicates.

Liz Chen: That pseudo looks fine but watch allocation on every request. Use an arena-backed fixed-size stack or a tiny bitmap if we can hash group ids. Also add metrics: dedupe_hits, dedupe_misses, avg_damp_factor.

Samir Patel: Need tests. Unit tests for: identical probe_id -> dampened; different probe -> unaffected; edge cases when probe_id missing -> fall back to fuzzy fingerprinting.

Mike Rosario: Rollout plan? We should not flip ingestion changes at once.

Elaine Ho: Proposed plan:
1) quick runtime guard behind feature-flag (canary 10% traffic) + telemetry (dedupe_hits, change in final_score distribution)
2) run simulation (policy-sim) to validate canonicalization rules against 7 days of history
3) RFC for ingestion-level canonicalizer (stream processor update) with migration mapping
4) phased ingestion rollout after sim and canary look good

Igor Kovacs: For runtime canary: add CPU budget and per-tenant opt-out. Also precompute group fingerprints to minimize work per-request.

Liz Chen: I'll add alerting and dashboards: show dedupe ratio by region/tenant and top probe_ids causing dampening. If dedupe ratio spikes -> orchestrate rollback.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline: policy-sanitization branch tests passed (unit + basic perf smoke). Build 3557 succeeded :white_check_mark:

Elaine Ho: Thanks. I'll write an RFC follow-up with the pseudocode, tests, and rollout checklist. Adding action items: @Samir to draft runtime patch, @Igor to evaluate perf impact, @Liz to prepare dashboards, @Mike to flag impacted customers.

Samir Patel: I'll open the PR for the runtime guard today and include perf bench results.

Igor Kovacs: Will run perf bench and report back by EOD tomorrow.

Liz Chen: Dashboard ETA: end of day next Tue.

Mike Rosario: I'll reach out to the two customers to give a heads-up and get context.

Elaine Ho: Great. Putting this thread as the working log. RFC link to follow once drafted. :thumbsup:
